source.title: DSIT Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025/2026
source.publication_date_evidence: Date stated on the inspected official source
source.reporting_period: UK eligible business/charity survey; August–December 2025 fieldwork; preceding 12 months per interview
source.reviewed_by: Codex source-content/rights review; no owner Evidence acceptance
source.review_notes: Original source inspected through approved web research tool; bounded reviewed excerpt only, not an original-file archive. Independent review correction: retained methodology/exclusions, weighting, large-business definition and recall window, not just headline estimates.
source.retrieval_extent: Located reviewed web passages; separators normalised for numerical rows; original bytes unavailable
source.limitation: Weighted self-reported survey estimates; August–December2025 fieldwork, preceding12months per interview. Identified/reported events only, not every hidden attack or a named bank incident. Aggregate prevalence remained in line with prior year.

excerpts.quote: Just over four in ten businesses (43%)
Overall prevalence of cyber breaches or attacks has remained in line with last year
medium (65%) and large (69%) businesses were more likely to have experienced a cyber breach or attack in the last 12 months compared to micro (42%) and small (46%) businesses.
The data for businesses and charities have been weighted to be statistically representative of these two populations.

Sole traders and public-sector organisations (excluding education) are outside the scope of the survey. In addition, businesses with no IT (Information Technology) capacity or online presence were deemed ineligible.
where organisations were asked about their cyber security experiences over the preceding 12 months.
The survey only includes the breaches or attacks that organisations were able to identify and willing to report.
